findings: Correctness: every raw-group hash site in the distinct radix HTs now goes through HashGroups. The radix sink reaches it through AddChunk(groups,payload,filter) at radix_partitioned_hashtable.cpp:573, and FindOrCreateGroups(groups,addresses,new_groups) also uses it. TryAddCompressedGroups, which hashes on its own, is skipped when the option is on. Combine/FlushMove (aggregate_hashtable.cpp:938), resize, repartition and spilling all reuse the stored hash column. So every tuple in one table gets the same hash function, and deduplication stays exact.

Column order: in DistinctAggregateData the grouping_set is an ordered std::set of group indices (< group_by_size) plus distinct child indices (>= group_by_size). The group columns therefore form a prefix of the distinct HT's columns, and partition_key_count = grouping_sets[i].size() covers exactly that prefix. SetPartitionKeyCount turns itself off unless the key is a strict prefix (layout ColumnCount()-1 = number of group columns).

Bit splice: only bits [36,48) (Mask(MAX_RADIX_BITS)) are replaced. Partition selection for any radix_bits <= 12 reads only those bits, and salt and pointer-table bits still come from the full hash. Probe quality is unchanged and partitioning is consistent across repartitioning.

Only distinct radix tables get the setting. The main HT, ungrouped DISTINCT, the empty grouping set, the window and recursive-CTE uses of GroupedAggregateHashTable, and the join correlated counts are all untouched.

The gate (estimated_cardinality >= 4096) depends on the planner estimate and the shape of the query, not on names, literals or this dataset. If the estimate is wrong, only performance suffers (partition skew); results stay correct.
Small and maintainable. No benchmark, settings or measurement code is touched.
